rule.text: Highest first-window mean lead over the average liquid stock, among versions with enough picks and a positive mean after a 0.49% round trip; within 0.05 points the one with fewer rules. The second window is printed whatever it shows.

month.what: The month list refuses a stock with no industry, and the replay handed the engine NSE's list as it stands today, so it could pick only companies in that list. Beside the lead over every liquid stock, its records measure the lead over the liquid stocks in that list: vs_eligible_pct (after the round trip, vs_eligible_net_pct; Newey-West t, vs_eligible_t) and lists_ahead_of_eligible_pct, with member_premium_pct, how far their average ran ahead of every liquid stock's over the same list dates, per hold. Those stocks are more than the list could pick: it also refuses an industry with too few liquid stocks to rank on money flow. Reported beside the rule, never used by it.

long.what: On every long list date. companies: the liquid companies listed a year that the engine ranks for the long list, less the ones it judges as lenders (a company with no filings counts as none, as the list reads it); with_filings: how many of them had any filing visible that session; and for each check, how many had its figure. most_from is the list date from which a figure was known for at least half of them on every list date after (None if not on the last); first_pct and second_pct are its mean share known over each window's list dates, and first_half_pct over the list dates of the record's first half (first_half), as the page splits the record.
